title: Exact-head one-shot review and safe stack restacking (#2557)
lane_outcome: Provide receipt-backed one-shot exact-head review and compare-and-swap stack restacking without weakening the merge gate.
purpose_for_parent: Closes the isolated review/publication workflow issue in a focused PR.
technical_strategy: Keep exact-head review requests in the existing repo-local controller and isolate stack rewrites in a declaration-driven command whose preflight, CAS pushes, optional metadata edits, and partial-write state are captured in one durable receipt.
technology_choices: Use full Git object IDs and explicit GitHub PR identities as all external mutation keys.
Use git rebase --onto in temporary worktrees and git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<old-head> for publication.
Keep merge authority and the persistent watcher lifecycle outside both commands.

acceptance_boundary: All lane slices have landed, lane proof aggregation is satisfied, and residual work is routed.
proof_strategy: Stopped-watcher, stale-review, idempotency, force-with-lease success/failure, and live bounded stack evidence.

evidence: Stopped-watcher, duplicate, atomic-claim, stale-request, and stale-result review fixtures pass.
Temporary bare-remote dry-run, exact-lease publication, PR metadata, failed lease, and preflight isolation fixtures pass.
The repo-owned review_stack_operations proof route reports sufficient-recorded for the product surface.
known_gaps: External reviewers may exit without posting a marker; the request remains durably awaiting-result and does not relaunch implicitly.
Multi-descendant publication is bounded and receipt-backed but cannot be atomic across GitHub refs.
